nodes.summary: For a graph $R$ (the row), the all-covered signature $\sigma_\bullet$ of $R$ is the signature that gives every vertex of $R$ the state covered; it is a signature because it has no uncovered vertex.

nodes.summary: For every finite graph $G$, the value at $1$ of the domination polynomial of $G$ equals the number of dominating sets of $G$.
nodes.title: The domination polynomial at one counts dominating sets

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $m$ and $n$, let $P_k$ denote the path on the vertices $0, \dots, k - 1$. Then the domination polynomial of the grid $P_m \mathbin{\square} P_{n+1}$ equals $\sum_\sigma G^\sigma(z)$, the sum running over the signatures $\sigma$ of the row graph $P_m$ with no uncovered vertex, where $G^\sigma(z)$ is the almost dominating polynomial of $P_m$ with $n + 1$ rows and last-row state $\sigma$.

nodes.title: Transfer-matrix formula for the domination polynomial of the grid

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $m$ and $n$ with $n \ge 1$, let $C_k$ denote the cycle graph on the vertices $0, \dots, k - 1$, in which distinct $i$ and $j$ are adjacent when $i - j \equiv \pm 1 \pmod k$, and let $\bar A$ be the domination transfer matrix of the row graph $C_m$. Then the domination polynomial of the torus $C_m \mathbin{\square} C_n$ equals the trace of $\bar A^n$.

nodes.summary: For a finite graph $G$, the domination polynomial of $G$ is the polynomial $\sum_S z^{|S|}$ with integer coefficients, the sum running over the dominating sets $S$ of $G$.
nodes.title: Domination polynomial

nodes.summary: For a simple graph $R$ on a vertex set $V$ (the row), a signature of $R$ is a map $\sigma$ assigning to each vertex of $V$ a domination state (uncovered, covered or occupied) such that $\sigma$ is a domination signature for $R$, that is, no uncovered vertex is adjacent in $R$ to an occupied vertex. This is the type of all signatures of $R$; when $R$ is a cycle they are the paper's cyclic signatures.
nodes.title: Signatures of a row graph

nodes.summary: A domination state is one of three labels: uncovered, covered or occupied.
nodes.title: Domination states

For every signature $\tau$ of $R$, the entry $A_{\tau\sigma_\bullet}$ equals $z^{\operatorname{occ}(\tau)}$, where $\operatorname{occ}(\tau)$ is the number of occupied vertices of $\tau$, if every covered vertex of $\tau$ is…

The transfer matrix $A$ of $R$ is the matrix with entries in $\mathbb{Z}[z]$, rows indexed by the new signature $\tau$ and columns by the old signature $\sigma$, both ranging over the signatures of $R$, whose entry $A_{\tau\sigma}$ is $z^{\operatorname{occ}(\tau)}$ if $\tau$ is compatible with $\sigma$ and $0$ otherwise; here $\operatorname{occ}(\tau)$ is…
nodes.title: Domination transfer matrix

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph and $S$ a finite set of vertices of $G$. Then $S$ dominates $G$ if and only if no vertex of $G$ has domination state uncovered relative to $S$ in $G$.
nodes.title: Dominating sets have no uncovered vertex

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a simple graph on a vertex set $V$ (the row). A map $\sigma$ assigning to each vertex of $V$ a domination state (uncovered, covered or occupied) is a signature for $R$ if no uncovered vertex is adjacent in $R$ to an occupied vertex: for all vertices $i, j$ adjacent in $R$, it is not the case that $\sigma(i)$ is uncovered and $\sigma(j)$ is occupied.
nodes.title: Domination signature

nodes.summary: For every simple graph $R$ on a finite vertex set, the number of occupied vertices of the all-covered signature of $R$ is $0$.
nodes.title: The all-covered signature has no occupied vertex

nodes.summary: Let $V$ be a finite set and let $\sigma$ assign a domination state (uncovered, covered or occupied) to each element of $V$. The occupied count $\operatorname{occ}(\sigma)$ is the number of elements $i \in V$ such that $\sigma(i)$ is occupied.
nodes.title: Number of occupied vertices

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph, $S$ a finite set of vertices of $G$ and $v$ a vertex of $G$. Then the domination state of $v$ relative to $S$ in $G$ is occupied if and only if $v \in S$.
nodes.title: A vertex is occupied exactly when it lies in the set

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph, $S$ a finite set of vertices of $G$ and $v$ a vertex of $G$. The domination state of $v$ relative to $S$ in $G$ is occupied if $v \in S$, covered if $v \notin S$ and $v$ is adjacent in $G$ to some vertex of $S$, and uncovered otherwise.
nodes.title: Domination state of a vertex

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
